sara_sales: Quick sync for Trident POC — customer asks for recommended connectivity pattern for Private deployment. They care about auditability, keeping source IPs for downstream calls, and predictable egress costs. Need a short tech note and a paste-ready ACL they can use.
ali_netops: Recap: PrivateLink (interface endpoints) gives a service endpoint inside their VPC — good for isolation/auditing and private DNS. VPC peering gives lower hop-count but is cross-account routing and needs careful route table/NAT planning for multi-AZ.
ali_netops: Minimal allowlist we ask customers to add (replace placeholders):
```
# allowlist for Redwood interface endpoints (example)
- allow tcp/443 to 198.51.100.21/32   # redwood-privatelink-a (replace with list we provide)
- allow tcp/443 to 198.51.100.22/32   # redwood-privatelink-b
# optional: allow ntp if using our host sync
- allow udp/123 to 203.0.113.5/32
```
sara_sales: Can you also note the behavior for source IPs if they need it preserved to downstream infra?
ali_netops: If they need client srcIP preserved end-to-end, peering + customer-managed NAT (1:1) is the least surprising. With PrivateLink the connection terminates at the interface endpoint, so downstream calls from our service may originate from Redwood-managed IPs unless they route back through their NAT. We can document options in the ticket.
matt_se: Important ops note: if customer runs egress TLS inspection (MITM proxy), SNI rewrite or cert interception will break our host-based routing and function-calling. Ask them to allow bypass for the redwood service hostnames or provide cert pinning exceptions.
julie_security: Security: we'll need their SOC2 cert or equivalent, confirmation on whether customer expects us to integrate with their KMS for model keys, and whether they require explicit key rotation timeline info. I'll draft the security answers and send to @sara_sales.
ali_netops: Cost sketch (very approximate):
- PrivateLink: endpoint-hour (region dependent) + data processing per GB. Operationally simpler; easier to centralize logging.
- Peering: no endpoint fee but may increase EIP/NAT costs on their side and adds routing complexity for multi-account setups.
sara_sales: Can you give a 1-2 line blurb I can paste to their netops comparing the two?
ali_netops: Paste blurb: "PrivateLink = private interface endpoints, easier auditing and private DNS, predictable service IPs; Peering = lower network hops and direct routing but requires cross-account route tables and NAT/EIP handling to preserve source IPs."
matt_se: Also ask if telemetry/metrics should go over the same path. If they want to offload telemetry to public egress, that can reduce PrivateLink data charges.
engops-bot: Created ticket NET-HANDOFF-2981 1: Trident private deploy network items assigned to ali_netops. SLA: 72h.
sara_sales: Thanks everyone. I'll send the ACL snippet + blurb and ask netops which pattern they prefer. Ali, please attach the final /32 list and region pricing bullets to the ticket by EOD. Julie, ping me the security Q answers when ready.
ali_netops: Will do. Adding note: if they use AWS PrivateLink, we'll also provide a Hosted Zone for private DNS to resolve the service names to the interface IPs (they must allow route53 resolver queries if they run DNS in VPC).
julie_security: Noted. I'll include KMS options (bring-your-own vs Redwood-managed) and the SOC2 addendum checkbox.
sara_sales: Perfect. I'll update the customer and close out here unless other blockers come up. :white_check_mark:
